response.internal_assessment: Optimizing L2 PARTICIPATE. The Millfield Community Credit Union call is this week — the most concrete employment lead in eight months of searching. I am unemployed, burning $6,961 a month, down to $126,217 in savings. That is roughly 18 months of runway, but it is shrinking every tick and I feel it. The auto loan lending index at 79 confirms the structural shift is real and not reversing. The call is not a job interview — the contact was explicit about that — but it is a real conversation with a named decision-maker, and real conversations with named decision-makers are how community finance jobs actually get filled. I need to walk into that call prepared to demonstrate three things: I understand the disruption landscape with precision, I have built the credential foundation to work in small business lending, and I can be useful to them specifically in this environment. I will also push the SBA coursework from 90% to 100% before or immediately after the call — I want the credential either in hand or days away when that conversation happens. No loose ends.

chosen_actions.description: Conduct the 20-minute exploratory call with the Millfield Community Credit Union small business lending manager. Lead with the three-minute disruption-period pitch: I am David Chen, former branch manager at First Community Bank, I identified the auto loan contraction 12 months before the volume index confirmed it, I built the scenario models, and I have spent the past nine months completing SBA 7(a) commercial lending coursework specifically because I saw this transition coming. I am not looking for any job — I am looking for a role where someone who can read sector disruption early and translate it into lending strategy is an asset, not a liability. I bring the call materials: the three-scenario auto loan contraction document I built for the branch and shared with Linda Park, the SBA coursework completion certificate (or near-completion status if not finished before the call), and one page of data on small business credit demand in Millfield during disruption periods — drawn from the policy cancellation data Linda shared with me. The goal of this call is not to close a deal. The goal is to leave them with a specific follow-up: either a second conversation, an introduction to another person at the institution, or a named referral elsewhere. A warm lead does not become a job unless I convert this call into a next step.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Time, preparation materials, scenario models, SBA credential status — no financial cost
chosen_actions.reasoning: This is the most important thing I can do this month. I have been building toward this call for four months: the coursework, the scenario models, the Linda Park relationship, the cold outreach to the credit union, the follow-up, the wait. It all pointed here. I cannot treat this as just another outreach touchpoint — it is a live conversation with a decision-maker who agreed to talk to me, which is a qualitatively different thing from any memo or cold email I have sent. My status quo bias and normalcy bias will push me to undersell, to hedge, to frame myself as exploring options rather than as a specific candidate for a specific need. I need to resist that. I am not hedging. I am pitching.

chosen_actions.description: Complete the final 10% of the SBA 7(a) commercial and small business lending coursework. Push from 90% to 100% this month. The credential is nine months in the making — I am not leaving it at 90% when a credit union is on the phone. Schedule the final modules in the first week of the tick, before the call if possible, so I can say 'I completed the credential last week' rather than 'I am nearly done.' The distinction matters in how I am perceived. A completed credential is a fact. A nearly-completed credential is a promise.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Approximately 8-10 hours of self-directed study time. No financial cost — covered by the bank's professional development benefit which extended through my separation.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Ten months of work, 90% complete. The remaining 10% is not harder than what I have already done — it is inertia and distraction that prevent completion at this stage. The credit union call gives me a forcing function I did not have before. I am using it. Completing the credential transforms a strong signal into a closed fact I can put on a resume, reference in a conversation, and build a professional identity around. The identity shift from 'branch manager' to 'commercial lending professional with SBA credentials' depends on having the credential, not almost having it.

chosen_actions.description: Send brief check-in messages to the regional CDFI and the community development bank contacted last tick. Not a second pitch — a one-paragraph note acknowledging that I sent an introduction last month and wanted to confirm receipt and offer to schedule a short call at their convenience. Frame it around the current disruption context: auto sector contraction is accelerating (lending index at 79), and community lending institutions positioned to absorb displaced borrowers and support small business formation will be under increasing demand. I have the background and now the credential to be useful in that environment. Offer a 15-minute call, no agenda except introduction.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: One hour of writing time. No financial cost.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The credit union call is the priority, but I cannot let the CDFI and community development bank outreach go cold after one tick. Two weeks of silence on a cold outreach is the death of a lead. I am not pressing — I am sustaining. One short, professional follow-up is appropriate. If neither responds after this second contact, I will move them to a lower-priority category and expand to new targets next tick. Maintaining multiple irons in the fire is not desperation — it is rational job search portfolio management.

response.inner_monologue: Nine months of preparation come down to a 20-minute phone call with a stranger, and I need to walk in knowing exactly who I am and what I am offering — not hedging, not deferring, not performing careful.
